paper.title: Map2Select: A Training-Free HD-Map Plug-In for Visual Token Selection in Driving VLMs
paper.subtitle: Let the map guide what the model sees.
paper.abstract: Map2Select uses projected HD maps as an external compute prior to retain complementary visual evidence at a fixed token budget, without adding map tokens or retraining the VLM. Map semantics guide a weighted feature-space coreset, while marginal utility allocates tokens across camera views. The result is a compact set of visual tokens that balances scene coverage and driving relevance.
paper.version_note: Based on the frozen Map2Select manuscript and supported evaluation artifacts from July 2026.

steps.title: Project the map
steps.description: Use the ego pose and camera calibration to project HD-map semantics into each view. Pool the driving relevance signals onto the model's visual token grid.

steps.title: Weight visual coverage
steps.description: Convert keep and drop priors to semantic density: μᵢ ∝ (1 + p_keepᵢ) / (1 + p_dropᵢ), normalized to mean one. Select a coreset that covers the normalized visual features with these weights.

steps.title: Allocate across views
steps.description: Assign the fixed token budget according to the marginal gain in weighted coverage. Cameras can receive different numbers of tokens while preserving the total budget.

steps.title: Use the existing VLM
steps.description: Pass the retained visual tokens to the driving VLM. Selection requires no task-specific retraining and introduces no extra map tokens.

method.objective: minimize ∑ᵢ μᵢ minⱼ∈S ‖zᵢ − zⱼ‖², subject to |S| = K
method.caption: The map supplies a prior over visual evidence; the coreset also accounts for feature diversity. Rectangles in the demo are selected visual tokens, not object detections or predicted lane boxes.
